subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw treat generic LiteLLM Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT responses as a recoverable provider/session error, and which recovery path should be the default?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing between provider-owned classification, compaction, fallback model routing, non-beta route guidance, or session cleanup can change provider and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
options.body: Require live LiteLLM/Vertex proof, then implement a scoped classifier and recovery message for that provider route only.

options.title: Broader generic INVALID_ARGUMENT recovery
options.body: Handle generic INVALID_ARGUMENT across providers, accepting higher risk of misclassifying unrelated validation failures.

options.title: Leave as manual reset guidance
options.body: Keep current generic failure behavior and document `/new` or model-route workarounds until more incidents prove a safe recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Require live LiteLLM/Vertex proof, then implement a scoped classifier and recovery message for that provider route only.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the adjacent provider-error normalization work and are the best available routing candidate for the provider failover policy choice.
